Definition: probably strengthened from G5420; a signet (as fencing in or protecting from misappropriation); by implication, the stamp impressed (as a mark of privacy, or genuineness), literally or figuratively:--seal.
BiblicalUsage: A seal is a mark of ownership and a closed book. The book in the right hand of Him on the throne is sealed with seven seals, Paul says the Corinthian believers are the seal of his apostleship, the foundation of God stands sure having this seal, The Lord knoweth them that are His, and Abraham received circumcision as a seal of the righteousness of faith.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the seal says whose we are and what is finished: the book is shut until the Lamb opens it, and the Lord knows His own. I hold that the seal on my life is the same mark: the Lord knoweth them that are His.
